column1: # rlxfw's boot marks, one row per line of Realtek's source that rlxfw changes.
# R3-6.   Applied and checked by: tools/rlxfw-marks.py
# baseline-drop: src-vendor/rtl819x-toolchain @ 5c9be5d9
# tree-root: the STAGED top, so paths cover both linux-2.6.30/ and boards/
# WHY THERE ARE ELEVEN OF THESE AND NOT ONE.
# 量, on the built R3 vmlinux: printk is a stub, early_printk is a WEAK EMPTY
# stub (16 bytes at 0x80013bec: sw a1,4(sp) / sw a2,8(sp) / jr ra / sw
# a3,12(sp)), and panic_printk reaches the wire only after a console is
# registered.  讀, this unit's own capture bench/2026-08-24c/G6.log: from
# `start address: 0x80003440` to `Realtek WLAN driver - version 1.6` there is
# NOTHING.  So a kernel that dies anywhere in start_kernel produces one
# capture -- `start address:` then silence -- whatever killed it.  R3's D3
# ("early bring-up completes") had no observable at all, and R3-8's first
# seating would have spent a power cycle to learn nothing.
# Each row below is placed to make one suspect readable as one line.  The rule
# for adding a row is: it must separate two causes that would otherwise share
# a capture.  A row that only says "we got further" is not worth a line of
# somebody else's source.
# WHAT MAKES THESE DISCRIMINATORS RATHER THAN LABELS.
# The anti-DoD (PROGRESS.md): 2026-08-25 a second `J 80500000` booted the
# VENDOR kernel, so a banner is not evidence.  These are constants, which is
# the weaker form -- but `rlxfw-marks.py verify` reads the built image AND the
# vendor's, and a constant absent from the vendor image cannot be printed by
# it.  B02 and B07 are the stronger form on top: their values are read out of
# this die at run time.
# COST.  38400 8N1 = 3,840 B/s. Eleven marks, mean 11 bytes -> ~32 ms of UART
# on a boot whose loader stage alone takes 348 ms (CLK-15). Not measurable.
# id
# The four rows that are not marks: my file has to reach the link, and the
# call sites need a prototype -- arch/rlx/kernel/Makefile carries
# `EXTRA_CFLAGS += -Werror`, so an implicit declaration is a build failure.
# The anchor for each include is a line that occurs exactly once in that file,
# which is checked rather than assumed.
MK
column6: rlxfw_mark.c is copied in by --src and needs a Kbuild line. It is placed immediately after early_printk.o on purpose: prom_putchar, the only function rlxfw_mark calls, is built by THAT line, so the dependency is visible in the file rather than only in the #error inside it. The anchor is written with single spaces and matched normalised, because Kbuild lines are tab-aligned and this file is tab-separated

column1: # Before any console exists.  This window is unreachable by CONFIG_PRINTK=y as
# well: setup_early_printk() does not run until arch/rlx/kernel/setup.c:546.

column6: the first mark, and the only claim that matters at D1/D2: the decompressor handed control over, the kernel is running C, and the UART the loader left behind still works. Placed after page_address_init() and before the printk(linux_banner) that is a stub in this configuration. Silence here with `start address:` printed means the image was entered and died before or inside start_kernel's prologue -- which RUNSHEET B03 records as TWO causes and this separates from the rest

brackets start_kernel's generic prologue -- boot_init_stack_canary, cgroup_init_early, local_irq_disable, tick_init, boot_cpu_init, page_address_init. Low suspicion (mainline generic), which is exactly why it is worth one line: if the ladder stops between B00 and B01 the fault is in code this port did not write, and that is a different day's work from a BSP fault

COMPUTED. cpu_probe() reads PRId and fills cpu_data[]; this prints the register itself. Two things at once: a hang inside cpu_probe (the CPU identification table, and arch/rlx/include/asm/cpu.h maps PRID_IMP_RLX4181 = 0xcd00) becomes readable, AND the value is a second, independent reading of CPU-04 -- 量 0x0000CD01 on 2026-08-25b through probe2's bare-metal CP0 census, which shares no code with this. The vendor image cannot fake it because it does not contain the string

bsp_init() is arch/rlx/bsp/prom.c and it computes mem_size by READING THE DRAM CONFIGURATION REGISTER at BSP_MC_MTCR0 -- bank/bus-width/row/column decode, live, on a board whose DRAM this project has never configured. The plan's `memory-related` failure case starts here, not at paging_init

column1: # Inside bsp_setup().  Three suspects in three consecutive statements, and the
# last one ends in a bare while(1).

column6: bsp_setup() entry. Brackets arch_mem_init's prologue, and it is the first mark in a file that is NOT under arch/rlx -- boards/rtl8196e/bsp/ is where arch/rlx/bsp points, and in two of the three drops that symlink dangles

THE DIVISOR. bsp_serial_init() runs early_serial_setup() on UART0 with s.uartclk = BSP_SYS_CLK_RATE, and prom_putchar never touches the divisor -- it inherits whatever is set. Every mark before this one rides the loader's 38400. If B00-B04 are clean and B05 is GARBAGE, the vendor's own serial init changed the line rate and nothing after it is readable at 38400; if B05 is missing entirely, early_serial_setup returned nonzero and panic()'d before any console existed to print the panic. Those are two different findings and this is the line that separates them

CPU-46's scratchpad. _imem_dmem_init() is the CP3 sequence this repo found at 0x80002210-0x80002300 in this unit's own kernel: set CU3, write 0x020, 0x202, load base+0x3FFF into CP3 $0/$1 (16 KiB I-MEM), issue 0x010, then base+0x1FFF into $4/$5 (8 KiB D-MEM). It is Lexra-specific, it is coprocessor 3, and CLAUDE.md's rule about measuring the ISA under Linux exists because of exactly this class. A hang between B05 and B06 names it

COMPUTED, and this is the single most valuable row in the file. The next four lines are `if (ret != 0) bsp_machine_halt();` and bsp_machine_halt() is `while(1);` -- a designed, silent, unrecoverable hang with no message anywhere. TC-23 already records the desk channel stopping at the switch-core probe, and this unit's own kernel stops there too. Printing ret turns the most likely silent death of the first boot into a number. If B07 prints a nonzero value and nothing follows, the gate has its answer in one power cycle

column1: # After the memory map, and after the console handover.

column6: bootmem_init, sparse_init and paging_init as one bracket. They are taken together on purpose: this project has no reason yet to prefer one of the three as a suspect, and three rows where one will do is how a ladder stops being read. If the boot stops between B03 and B08 the next session splits this row, and the reason for splitting it will be a capture

the handover. Everything before this reached the wire only through prom_putchar; from here the registered console is up and, in the `loud` variant, printk output starts. B09 is therefore the line that says which instrument the rest of the capture is coming from -- and if the loud variant prints B09 and then nothing while the quiet one keeps going, the fault is in the console path, which is the one area R3-6 owns

init_post(), immediately before the branch that decides HOW userspace is reached. ramdisk_execute_command is set only when an initramfs was unpacked and /init exists (init/main.c:885-891); if it is NULL the kernel falls through to /sbin/init, /etc/init, /bin/init, /bin/sh and then panics. Decision B's refutation condition is `the initramfs fails to unpack`, and B10 followed by M4 is that condition answered, while B10 followed by silence or by a panic is it answered the other way

column1: # 🆕 P4a, 2026-09-01.  ONE ROW THAT IS NOT A LADDER MARK, AND THE FILE'S OWN
# RULE FOR ADDING A ROW DOES NOT APPLY TO IT.
# The rule above -- *a row must separate two causes that would otherwise share
# a capture* -- is about the boot ladder, and ID0 separates nothing.  It exists
# because P4a froze the build stamp.
# 量 2026-09-01: two builds of one tree, 49 s apart, differed in 84 of
# 3,935,472 bytes and every one of them was a clock reading.  Six were the
# kernel's UTS_VERSION, which PROGRESS.md's anti-DoD names as one of the three
# strings the vendor image cannot produce: `(key@K) ... #1 Fri Aug 28 23:37:47
# CST 2026`.  Freezing the clock does not delete that leg -- `(key@K)` is
# inside it -- but it removes the leg's SECOND role: saying which of my builds
# is running, read off the console, on the board.
# 🔴 Nothing else in the image had that role.  B00..B10 are constants and
# `start address: 0x80003600` is a property of the link, so both are the same
# for every build of mine.  Before this row, a frozen stamp would have left the
# board unable to distinguish today's image from last week's -- and 2026-08-25
# is the record of what that costs: a second `J 80500000` booted the VENDOR
# kernel and the banner looked like a pass.
# WHAT THE VALUE IS.  `RLXFW_SRC_ID`, defined by tools/rlxfw-kbuild.sh as
# KCPPFLAGS, is the first 8 hex of a sha256 over every file under config/,
# hashed with paths RELATIVE to the repository root.  So it is a function of
# the declaration and of nothing else: it moves when the recipe moves, it is
# the same on any machine, and it needs no remembering -- which is the one
# thing config/rlxfw-build-stamp does need.
# ⚠️ WEAKER THAN B02/B07 AND THE SAME KIND AS B00..B10.  It is compiled in, not
# read off this die at run time.  What makes it a discriminator is
# `rlxfw-marks.py verify`: present exactly once in my image, absent from the
# vendor's.
# ⚠️ IT MOVES A MEASURED NUMBER.  The ladder was eleven marks and 139 bytes on
# the wire (量 2026-08-30, bench/2026-08-30b block 1).  A build carrying this
# row prints a twelfth line, `RLXFW-ID0=XXXXXXXX`, so SPEC.md FW-32's 849 bytes
# describes `quietm`, which does not have it, and the NEXT image's byte count
# is a new measurement rather than that one.
# ⚠️ A --marks BUILD WITHOUT -DRLXFW_SRC_ID DOES NOT COMPILE.  That is the
# intended failure: a build failure rather than an image whose identity string
# is wrong.  The driver always passes it.
ID0
column6: IDENTITY, not a ladder step. The recipe's own sha256, printed on the board immediately after the banner it is there to make up for -- a reader sees the frozen stamp and the thing that identifies the build on consecutive lines. Anchored on the banner printk because it occurs exactly once in main.c and because B00's anchor is one line above it, so the ladder still opens with B00.
